A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BINGO framework despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, reward ablations, training analyses, and comparisons across reinforcement-learning algorithms.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds extended-decoding evaluations and numerical hyperparameter comparisons.

M1.justification: The LLMLingua-2 significance estimator, cosine reward, dynamic length schedule, and PPO objective remain. V2 introduces a generic scoring-function notation but retains the same estimator in Appendix C; this does not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and evaluate on MATH500, GSM8K, TheoremQA, and AIME2024. The added experiments vary decoding and hyperparameters within this existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes the frozen Base comparator from the length-reward comparison, although its results remain in Table 2. PPO, O1-Pruner, Kimi-k1.5, Efficient Reasoning, Demystifying, and DAST otherwise retain their participation.

E3.justification: New Appendix H adds a substantial evaluation protocol: a 32,768-token limit, three responses per prompt, temperature 0.6, and top-p 1.0. The selected incorrect-response reward weights change from 2 and 3 in v1 Table 6 to 5 and 5 in v2 Table 7; GSM8K's reported test count also changes from 1,320 to 1,319. These revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds robustness testing under longer, stochastic decoding. Appendix Q adds accuracy and length measurements for four hyperparameter combinations, whereas v1 Appendix O only listed settings and search ranges. Existing reward ablations, training analyses, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies independent experimental-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing shaded training plots retain their reporting. V2's three responses per prompt specify decoding sample size rather than independent-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds a full four-benchmark result table for extended decoding and numerical hyperparameter results. Table 1 also revises O1-Pruner's TheoremQA accuracy/length/L-Acc from 32.4/485/31.4 to 28.6/524/27.6. Most original results remain unchanged; the extended-decoding scores are additional results under different conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix D corrects v1's reversed significant/insignificant token-set inequalities to agree with the method. Appendix E replaces the initial zero penalty in its formal schedule with a negative constant, aligning it with the existing exploration argument. The principal assumptions, theorem, and proof approach remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that significance-aware and dynamic length rewards improve the accuracy–efficiency trade-off through BINGO. The new title and rewritten abstract emphasize the token-level perspective already central to v1.

C2.justification: V2 substantially refocuses the limitations, removing v1's specific discussion of token-significance bias, over-pruning, domain-specific failures, and deployment safeguards. It emphasizes PPO compatibility and training cost instead, adds a fluency-preservation explanation, and interprets the new experiments as supporting decoding and hyperparameter robustness. Appendix H also reports approximately fivefold computational overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly specifies decoding settings and training GPU counts, and revises inference hardware from eight to two H100 GPUs. Replacing the old hyperparameter table removes details including microbatch size, gradient accumulation, warm-up, and weight decay. New Appendix B asserts anonymous code and supplemental ZIP availability, but the claimed abstract link is absent and the ZIP cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cui et al.'s work on the entropy mechanism of reinforcement learning and removes the original LLMLingua citation by Jiang et al. The related-work discussion is condensed, while its central positioning against existing length-reward approaches remains.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, condenses related work and experimental exposition, and reorganizes the token-significance explanation. It also replaces the opening appendix sections and brings a rewritten limitations discussion into the main document.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout and introduces a new conceptual Figure 1. V1's performance-overview Figure 1 moves to v2 Appendix I as Figure 5. Tables and figures are extensively rearranged, with a new decoding-results table and a redesigned hyperparameter-results table.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the central efficiency claim through longer stochastic-decoding tests and measured hyperparameter sensitivity, while correcting two internal mathematical inconsistencies. These provide a limited net improvement over v1. The gains are tempered by removed implementation settings and specific failure-mode limitations, which weaken reproducibility and qualification of the claims.
